extracted.intended_audience: TeX/Plain-TeX users who define fonts and macros and need precise math-typesetting rules (macro writers, font designers, advanced TeX users)
extracted.subtask_description: Precise technical rules from Plain TeX (Appendices F and G) about font metrics, symbol classes, and the algorithm TeX uses to convert math lists into boxes; intended for people defining fonts/macros or debugging math layout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Font-family conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: TeX assumes family 0 contains normal roman fonts and families 1, 2, and 3 contain math italic, math symbol, and math extension fonts respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign symbolic names and mathchardefs accordingly; use the family assignment so TeX chooses the right glyphs for math text, symbols, and extensible pieces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Math-symbol font parameter requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Math symbol fonts (family 2) are required to have at least 22 \fontdimen parameters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plain TeX will not typeset a formula unless \textfont2, \scriptfont2, and \scriptscriptfont2 each contain at least 22 \fontdimen parameters; if a font has fewer parameters, assign extra parameters immediately after loading the font (intervening parameters default to zero).

rubrics_metrics.name: Math-extension font parameter requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Math extension fonts (family 3) must have at least 13 \fontdimen parameters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As with family 2, ensure \textfont3/\scriptfont3/\scriptscriptfont3 include the required parameters or assign additional values after loading.

rubrics_metrics.name: General fontdimen meanings and magnification behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Each font has at least seven \fontdimen parameters whose meanings include slant, interword space, x-height, quad (em width), and extra space added at sentence end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical numeric values provided for cmr10/cmmi10/etc.; when a font is magnified (via at or scaled), all fontdimen parameters except slant are magnified when the font is loaded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typewriter font (cmtt10) characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: cmtt10 is monospaced: every character and the interword space have width 0.5em; ligatures are absent (except specified), and some diacritics/characters are omitted or relocated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TeX inserts two spaces at the end of each sentence in typewriter font by default; change spacing conventions by assigning nonzero values to \spaceskip and \xspaceskip or by setting appropriate \fontdimen parameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Math-italic font (cmmi10) content and skewchar
rubrics_metrics.description: cmmi10 contains lowercase and uppercase Greek and modified non-Greek italics for mathematics; plain TeX takes comma, period, and slash from cmmi10 in math mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set the font's \skewchar to "177 for correct positioning of math accents with cmmi10.

rubrics_metrics.name: Math-symbol font (cmsy10) skewchar for calligraphic caps
rubrics_metrics.description: cmsy10 is the math symbol font used for \cal and contains symbols used with class assignments; its \skewchar should be set to '060 so math accents position properly over calligraphic capitals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the specified skewchar to ensure accents align correctly over calligraphic letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Math-extension font (cmex10) purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: cmex10 includes large symbols and components that can be assembled to build arbitrarily large delimiters and signs (e.g., large parentheses, square roots, braces).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The font metric encodes series of linked characters (successors) allowing TeX to build extensible delimiters; understand the component codes for constructing tall delimiters and radicals.

rubrics_metrics.name: TeX loads only font metric (tfm) info
rubrics_metrics.description: When TeX loads a font it uses only the metric information (heights, widths, depths, italic corrections, ligature and kerning info, and series/successor data), not the actual glyph shapes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metric files specify which characters form series and successors that TeX uses when selecting delimiter sizes; font design should supply correct tfm metrics even if gf/ps shapes differ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delimiter selection/search algorithm
rubrics_metrics.description: To set a variable delimiter TeX searches first for the 'small character' a in family f (in scriptscript, then script, then text size), then for the 'large character' b in family y; it checks whether a character has sufficient height+depth or is extensible; if none suitable are found the character with greatest height+depth is chosen; if no characters exist x is set to an empty box of width \nulldelimiterspace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an extensible character is found, TeX builds a vbox from pieces; if a character is chosen as an hbox its italic correction is included in the width.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reboxing to a specified width
rubrics_metrics.description: To rebox a given box to a specified width TeX unpacks the box (unless it was a vbox), adds a kern for any implied italic correction, inserts \hss glue at both left and right, and repackages the horizontal list into an hbox.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This method is used to equalize widths (e.g., numerator and denominator), centering the smaller unless infinite glue is present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Math symbol classification and math-mode-only rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Math symbols divide into classes (Ord, Op, Bin, Rel, Open, Close, Punct) and, unless stated otherwise, math symbols are available only in math modes; using a math symbol (like \alpha) in horizontal mode triggers an error and TeX will attempt to insert a $.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Call symbols by name (control sequence) to keep manuscripts adaptable across fonts; be mindful of symbol classes because TeX spaces differently depending on class.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of dotless i/j for accents
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \imath and \jmath (dotless i and j) when i and j are accented to avoid double dots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.g., $\hat\imath$ yields the correct accented i without the dot; similarly for j.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digits variants selection
rubrics_metrics.description: To get italic, boldface, or oldstyle digits use grouping with font switches: {\it0123456789}, {\bf0123456789}, {\oldstyle0123456789}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These conventions apply inside and outside math mode.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large operators vs binary operations distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: Large operators (\sum, \prod, \coprod, \int, etc.) come in two sizes for text and display styles and typically occur at the beginning of a formula and are subscripted; binary operations (\cup, \cap, \oplus, etc.) are smaller, occur between operands, and are rarely subscripted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not confuse large operators with similarly named smaller symbols (\Sigma, \Pi, \amalg, \smallint); choose the correct symbol class to get proper sizing and limit placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negation with \not and special negated names
rubrics_metrics.description: \not is a relation character of width zero that overlays the relation that follows it (e.g., \not\in yields a slashed-in symbol), but positioning may not be ideal for all relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use special control sequences (e.g., \notin) defined in Appendix B when a better slashed/crossed variant is desired; \not positioning can vary because relation symbols differ in width.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate symbol names and aliasing
rubrics_metrics.description: Plain TeX provides several alternate names for commonly used symbols (e.g., \ne and \neq, \le and \leq, \to and \rightarrow); you may also alias names yourself (e.g., \let\cupcap=\asymp).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use alternate names for convenience or readability; aliases allow portable naming preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalty insertion behavior (line-breaking helpers)
rubrics_metrics.description: When typesetting formulas inside paragraph text TeX inserts penalty items after binary operations and relations to aid line breaking; such penalties are not inserted in other contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This behavior applies when converting math lists to horizontal lists with penalties enabled; display formulas and subformulas use different rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Math starting styles and related style operations
rubrics_metrics.description: There are eight math styles in decreasing order D > D' > T > T' > S > S' > SS > SS'; C denotes the current style, C' is the primed variant, Ci is the superscript style of C, and C+ is the subscript style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The starting style for a formula determines the styles used unless overridden by style items; many translation rules refer to C, C', Ci, C+ when selecting fonts and sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1: Leave certain items unchanged
rubrics_metrics.description: If the current math-list item is a rule or discretionary or penalty or 'whatsit' or boundary item, leave it unchanged and move to the next item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These items are passed through during the first pass of translation from math list to horizontal list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 2: Glue and kern translation
rubrics_metrics.description: If the current item is glue or a kern: if it is glue from \nonscript and the immediately following item is glue or a kern, remove that item if C ≤ S; otherwise, if the glue/kern is from \mskip or \mkern convert from mu units to absolute units by multiplying each finite dimension by the appropriate mu-to-point factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handle \mskip/\mkern (mu units) specially by converting to absolute dimensions depending on the current math unit scale before moving on.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 3: Style-change item handling
rubrics_metrics.description: If the current item is a style change, set C to the specified style, delete the current item from the list, and continue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Style-change items switch the current math style and are not represented in the resulting horizontal list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 4: Four-way choice handling
rubrics_metrics.description: If the current item is a four-way choice (contains four sublists for the four main styles), replace it with the sublist that corresponds to the current style C and continue processing from that point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Four-way choice items allow TeX to select the appropriate subformulas per current style (display, text, script, scriptscript).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 5: Bin class correction at list boundaries
rubrics_metrics.description: If the current item is a Bin atom and it is the first atom in the list or the most recent previous atom was Bin, Op, Rel, Open, or Punct, change the current Bin to Ord and continue with Rule 14; otherwise continue with Rule 17.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This enforces proper spacing by reclassifying Bin to Ord in contexts where a binary operator would be syntactically incorrect (e.g., at the start of a formula or after another operator).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 6: Previous Bin correction before Rel/Close/Punct
rubrics_metrics.description: If the current item is a Rel or Close or Punct atom and the most recent previous atom was Bin, change that previous Bin to Ord and continue with Rule 17.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents incorrect spacing where a Bin would appear immediately before a relational/closing/punctuation atom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 7: Open or Inner items
rubrics_metrics.description: If the current item is an Open or Inner atom, go directly to Rule 17 (the main packaging/boxing rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open/Inner atoms are handled in the general atom-to-box translation rules rather than the Bin/Rel corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 8: \vcenter atom handling
rubrics_metrics.description: If the current item is a vcenter atom, let its nucleus be a vbox of height+depth v; change the height to v+a and the depth to v-a where a is the axis height; change this atom to type Ord and continue with Rule 17.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This centers the vbox on the math axis and ensures it behaves like an ordinary atom for subsequent processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 9: Over atom (\overline) construction
rubrics_metrics.description: If the item is an Over atom (\overline), set box x to the nucleus in style C'; replace the nucleus with a vbox built as: kern e, hrule of height e, kern 3e, and box x from top to bottom, where e is the default rule thickness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This places a rule above the nucleus with specified clearances (3e) and accounts for e units of extra whitespace assumed above the rule; continue with subsequent boxing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 10: Under atom (\underline) construction
rubrics_metrics.description: If the item is an Under atom (\underline), set box x to the nucleus in style C; replace the nucleus by a vtop made from box x, kern 3e, and hrule of height e, where e is the default rule thickness, and add e to the depth of the box.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This puts a rule under the nucleus with the same clearances used for Over atoms, and updates the depth accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 11: Radical (\radical / \sqrt) construction
rubrics_metrics.description: If the current item is a Radical atom, set box x to the nucleus in style C'; compute e and p (e = font default rule thickness, p depends on style), set minimal clearance and obtain a variable delimiter whose height+depth ≥ h(x)+d(x)+clearance+e; set e to the height of the delimiter to use as the rule thickness; adjust clearance if delimiter depth exceeds content; construct a vbox consisting of kern e, hrule height e, kern (some amount), and the content box.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The algorithm ensures proper spacing between the radical sign's rule and the radicand, chooses a delimiter of adequate size (possibly extensible), and uses font-provided rule thickness (the radical character baseline aligns with the bottom of the rule).
